title: Snack Scout: Neon Hall Snack Dash
premise: A mobile-first top-down snack scavenger game set in a neon-lit school, where the player roams hallways and classrooms collecting five lunches while meeting campus characters and swapping between four playable scouts.
interaction_model: Touch-and-drag virtual joystick movement with tap controls for sound toggle and character switching; pickups and NPC conversations trigger automatically by proximity.
objective: Explore the campus map and collect all 5 lunch items to complete the run.
progression: Single-run arcade loop: start screen -> free exploration and collection across a procedurally generated school map -> win screen after all five lunches are collected -> optional replay with respawned items and NPC placement.
theme: Neon school scavenger hunt with anthropomorphic student characters and light social chatter.
mood: Playful, bright, cozy, lightly competitive, and arcade-like.
likely_audience: Casual mobile players, younger arcade/exploration fans, and players who enjoy light collection games with character flavor.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core loop because the entire movement, scoring, map generation, and win condition are visible in one file.
Moderate confidence in the final branding because the document title and start-screen title differ.
High confidence that character switching is cosmetic/flavor only, since it changes quotes and UI name but not stats or mechanics.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first top-down exploration game called "Snack Scout: Neon Hall Snack Dash" set inside a stylized neon boarding school with a central glowing hallway and many small classrooms branching off both sides. The player controls a cute anthropomorphic student scout using a large touch-and-drag virtual joystick only, with no keyboard dependence, and must roam the campus collecting exactly five lunch items hidden around the map to finish the run. Build the level as a tall tile-based school interior with repeated classroom rows, doors into each room, lockers lining corridor walls, classroom furniture like tables, chairs, and chalkboards, and collision that blocks walls, lockers, tables, and boards while still allowing movement through doors and around chairs. Use a camera that smoothly follows the player around a map larger than the screen, and render everything in bright pixel-art or faux-pixel style with neon blues, purples, pinks, and cyan highlights. Include four swappable playable characters with different names and appearances but identical movement mechanics; tapping a switch button should cycle the current character portrait/name and show a short flavor quote. Populate classrooms with many NPC students who do not need deep AI but should display short ambient dialogue automatically when the player walks near them, making the school feel social and lively. Place lunch pickups randomly on valid walkable spots away from the starting area, collect them automatically on contact, increment a visible HUD counter from 0/5 to 5/5, and add juicy feedback like pickup sounds, spark particles, and a small celebratory animated reaction overlay. Add a start screen that explains the mission in a concise arcade style, a top HUD with current character name and collection count, sound toggle and character swap buttons, and a win screen that appears immediately after the fifth lunch is collected with upbeat audio and a replay button. Keep the overall experience short, readable, cheerful, replayable, and optimized for touch screens, with the main loop being explore the corridor, enter rooms, gather lunches, hear quick campus chatter, and finish the snack run.
